claims.text: The proposed approach can compute lattice and electronic thermal conductivity separately in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed approach will predict total thermal conductivity within ±20% of experiment over 50–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The modeled HfNbTaTiZr state is nearly ideal and defect-free.
Applicable processed HfNbTaTiZr samples typically contain about 1 wt.% oxygen.
DFT-derived elastic and force constants can be used to model phonon transport in this alloy.
Electronic-structure calculations combined with Boltzmann transport theory can provide an electronic contribution distinct from the lattice contribution.
Electronic heat transport is predominant in HfNbTaTiZr at 50–200 K.
Lattice anharmonicity becomes increasingly important at high temperature, particularly in material containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Atomic-scale structure and impurity content determine phonon-scattering rates.
Atomic-scale structure and impurity content determine electronic band dispersion.
Explicitly representing phonon-phonon interactions and electronic band characteristics avoids conflating lattice and electronic conduction.
Avoiding conflation of the two transport channels will produce more reliable total-conductivity predictions.
The proposed approach will reduce prediction error by at least 15–20% relative to previous models.
Previous models merged lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
The dominant heat-transport channel shifts from electronic at low temperature to lattice at high temperature.
Previous analytical and DFT-based approximations generally deviated from measured thermal conductivity by more than 20%.
Significant defects, phase segregation, or departures from ideal HfNbTaTiZr composition place a sample outside the model's applicability regime.
Defect scattering and oxygen-induced changes to electronic structure may reduce the model's accuracy in real samples.
